result:
A couple of things I want to flag before drafting this, since a change record is the audit trail people will point to if the deploy goes wrong:

**The CI evidence needs to match the actual merge commit.** You rebased onto main last night (picking up the queue-timeout fix) and re-pushed, but build #9012 — was that CI run *after* the re-push, on the post-rebase HEAD? Rebasing changes the SHA even when the diff content doesn't change, and now the tree includes someone else's queue-timeout fix too. If #9012 ran on the pre-rebase commit, it's not actually evidence for what's about to be merged — it's evidence for a commit that no longer exists. Can you confirm the build ran on the current HEAD's SHA (and paste that SHA or the CI run link)?

**Priya's approval — same question.** "This morning" is ambiguous relative to "rebased last night." If her approval predates the rebase, GitHub will usually show it as stale/dismissed depending on branch protection settings, but I'd rather you confirm than assume.

Separately: I don't have anything to write into here — this directory is empty and I don't see a change-record template, system, or prior examples of "Quick change records" for this repo. Can you point me to where these live (a repo, a doc template, an internal tool) or paste the format you use? Once I have that plus the SHA/CI-run confirmation above, I can draft it in a couple minutes — plenty of time before 5pm.

I'd rather not write "fully tested and ready to merge" into a record until the CI-run-to-commit match is confirmed, since that's the one claim in this that's easy to get subtly wrong and matters if anything goes sideways after deploy.
